t:
Title 32, United States Code, is amended as follows:

    (1) 
Section 305 is amended by—

        (A) 
striking out “Except as provided in subsection (b), only male persons selected from the” and inserting in place thereof “The” in subsection (a);
 
        (B) 
striking out the first sentence of subsection (b); and
 
        (C) 
striking out “However, to” and “woman” in the second sentence of subsection (b) and inserting in place thereof “To” and “person”, respectively.
  
    (2) 
Section 313(b) is amended by inserting “and” after the semicolon in clause (1), striking out and” at the end of clause (2) and inserting a period in place thereof, and striking out clause (3).

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to Title 32, striking and inserting words to remove sex-based restrictions on National Guard appointments. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision. There is no tempting participation keyword here.

qwen_block.w: This section describes technical amendments to the text of Title 32 of the U.S. Code, specifically changing gender-specific language to gender-neutral language regarding personnel selection. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards with non-federal members, or other forms of participation as defined. The changes are purely editorial and administrative within the federal government's internal statutes.
qwen_block.s: Section 305 is amended by— (A) striking out “Except as provided in subsection (b), only male persons selected from the” and inserting in place thereof “The” in subsection (a); (B) striking out the first sentence of subsection (b); and (C) striking out “However, to” and “woman” in the second sentence of subsection (b) and inserting in place thereof “To” and “person”, respectively.

opus.w: This section only edits the wording of Title 32: it removes gender restrictions and strikes a clause. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. The phrase "selected from" is about who is eligible, not about outsiders taking part in a federal decision.
opus.s: striking out “Except as provided in subsection (b), only male persons selected from the” and inserting in place thereof “The” in subsection (a);
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** The only tempting reading would come from the section's "selected from" language, which could suggest some outside selection process. That reading doesn't hold up. The section only makes technical amendments to Title 32 (the National Guard title). It removes the "only male persons" restriction and gendered wording ("woman" becomes "person"), and it strikes a clause from section 313(b). No party outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, placed on an advisory body, or given a right to sue. No rulemaking is required either.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section describes legislative amendments to the text of Title 32 of the U.S. Code, specifically changing eligibility language from gender-specific terms to gender-neutral terms. It does not establish any process for the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The changes are substantive statutory edits, not procedural participation mechanisms.
qwen_chat.s: Section 305 is amended by— (A) striking out “Except as provided in subsection (b), only male persons selected from the” and inserting in place thereof “The” in subsection (a); (B) striking out the first sentence of subsection (b); and (C) striking out “However, to” and “woman” in the second sentence of subsection (b) and inserting in place thereof “To” and “person”, respectively.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing "male persons" to "person" or "woman" to "person" involves public participation because it expands the pool of people eligible for service, potentially involving public input. However, this is a substantive change to eligibility criteria, not a procedural requirement for the government to consult with outsiders before making a decision. The text describes legislative amendments to statutory language, not a process of consultation, hearing, or advisory committee involvement.
